text:
Sam: quick thread: I ran the max-token-pool sweep across cardsets (A10/T4/L4/A100/H100) to tune our continuous-batching heuristics.
Jia: awesome — what metric did you optimize for? p50 latency or tokens/sec?
Sam: primary objective was 99th percentile tail latency under mixed short+long workload, secondary is tokens/sec. also tracked KV cache fragmentation.
Maria: summary pls. TL;DR numbers are helpful.
Sam: TL;DR: A100/H100 safe with larger pools (max_tokens_per_batch=4096) -> no regression, throughput +12% for long tails. A10/T4 sweet spot around 2048. L4 behaved oddly: >1024 pooled tokens triggered a kernel selector flip to an int8 path that increased ctx copy time and KV fragmentation -> p99 up by ~140ms.
Ryan: can you paste the config you used and profiling output for L4? suspect kernel fit threshold is off.
Sam: paste: ```
{"policy": "token_pool", "targets": {"A100": 4096, "H100": 4096, "A10": 2048, "T4": 2048, "L4": 1024}, "queue_window_ms": 8, "burst_credit": 250}
```
Sam: perf snippet for L4 (single-run flame): ```
[profiling] model=redwood-v2, card=L4, batch_tokens=2048
kernel_select: chosen=fp16_int8_mixed (fallback prob=0.82)
kv_cache_frag: prefix_hits=0.74, avg_frag_payload_kb=18
token_emit: p50=5.8ms/token, p99=48.2ms/token
ctx_copy: total=210ms (↑65ms vs baseline)
``` 
Jia: oof — the kernel selector flip is the key. Looks like kernel-fit heuristics pick mixed-int8 for longer batches on L4 which pays off on raw matmul but costs in memory copy and KV locality.
Maria: any hypothesis why A10/T4 don't show the same flip at 2048? maybe kernel thresholds are per-arch but selector mistakenly uses a default threshold for L4.
Ryan: I instrumented selector heuristics before — there's a per-arch kernel_threshold table but we fallback to a generic heuristic when shape distribution is sparse. Could be we missed L4 in the kernel-fingerprint whitelist.
perf-bot: perf regression alert created: PR#5234, tag=regression/L4-kernelflip, linked-to=2468101214
Sam: experiment notes: when we force selector to prefer fp16 kernels on L4 via override (quick test): p99 drops to ~28ms/token and ctx_copy drops ~60ms. throughput slightly lower for very long sequences but overall SLA better.
Jia: tradeoff acceptable. For mixed workloads we should bias toward fp16 if KV cache usage > 50% to reduce fragmentation.
Maria: proposal: add a per-arch override map + dynamic override rule: if observed kv_cache_frag > 0.6 and avg_batch_tokens > 512 then prefer fp16 family. Also lower kernel_select length_threshold for L4 by 25%.
Ryan: also we should add a safety cap: max_tokens_per_batch enforced by card not just global policy — that prevents accidental scaling beyond local memory characteristics. config like: `card_limits: {L4:1024, A10:2048, T4:2048, A100:4096, H100:4096}`
Sam: added to experiment doc; I'll roll a canary with these adjustments to staging (50 nodes L4) and run the same mixed-suite for 4 hours overnight.
perf-bot: scheduled perf job #2468101214-01: workload=mixed-short-long, duration=4h, target=staging-L4
Jia: thanks. If staging looks good, we should push a gradual rollout with canary ramp and a fallback to lower pool sizes.
Maria: reminder: add evals to catch quality regressions when changing kernel family (int8 -> fp16 can change logits slightly). link to eval harness: https://ci.redwood/ev/harness
Ryan: will add a tiny regression check: KL-divergence on top-10 tokens + deterministic seed.
Sam: action items: (1) force override + threshold tweak for L4 in canary, (2) add per-card max_tokens to policy, (3) add perf & KL checks to pipeline, (4) watch KV fragmentation metrics. I'll post results in this thread tomorrow.
Maria: :thumbsup:
Sam: thanks — cc @Jia @Ryan for followups.
